FloorDivAny's float lane was math.Floor(a/b); CPython's float_floordiv is fmod-based. Past 2^53 the division rounds across an integer boundary the remainder does not: 2.543036645110022e16 // 3 is 8476788817033405.0 in CPython and 8476788817033407 through a floored division — two whole units. Reaching it needs total_tokens past 2^53, which is why a 3M-draw search under 1e6 finds nothing. FIRST FIX ATTEMPT WAS WRONG: it ported the fmod half and omitted the sign correction, passing every positive case and failing -3001.0 // 3 (-1000.0 vs -1001.0). The existing analyze differential caught it.

The call-site comment mapped EVERY pyval.LoadsMap error onto `except: continue`. Behaviour is a standing deliberate divergence already named at pyval.go's LoadsMap; the call-site comment contradicted it. Comment corrected; whether to match the abort is FILED, not decided.

SpendToday discarded ReverseReadline's error with `_ =` and returned the PARTIAL sum. CPython wraps the whole `for line in _reverse_readline(path)` loop in spend_today's outer `except Exception: return 0.0`, and _reverse_readline's fh.read sits INSIDE its while loop — so a mid-read I/O failure propagates past the partial total and the answer is 0.0. Direction is INVERTED from the usual one and still wrong: here CPython invents the smaller number (0.0 vs a real partial), so matching it makes the daily budget gate less conservative — fidelity is the contract. Found by the mutant-derivation pass reading the file closely, not by the review.

The thirty-seven in the differential-blind-spot paragraph is kept as a record of that day's measurement and now says so.

config.memory_dir() MKDIRS as a side effect of resolving a path, and run_health_probes spells its critical section `with locked_write(_snapshot_path())` — so CPython creates memory/ while still evaluating the ARGUMENT, before the load and before the probe loop. The port had SnapshotPath as a pure filepath.Join with the only MkdirAll inside WriteSnapshot, AFTER every probe. Measured: a workspace whose memory/ cannot be created gives CPython ran=0, silent=[], ZERO probes called; the port ran all of them. 47 fixtures shared an unstated assumption that memory/ already existed (C45/C46 chmod an EXISTING dir). Fixed by moving the mkdir into SnapshotPath (now returning an error), LoadSnapshot too, plus a shape-faithful pre-check in RunAndPersist; pinned by C48 (chmod) and C49 (a FILE where the dir belongs, so it survives a root test runner).

canon rendered every json.Number through Float64(), so two integers differing only past 2^53 compared EQUAL — on `cycle`, the field this module guarantees grows. No FIXTURE can catch this: canon runs over both sides, so a lossy transform applied to two agreeing sides leaves them agreeing (S8/S9 passed against the broken canon). Fixed by canonicalising numbers to a "num:"-prefixed text — the prefix stops the number 1 and the string "1" colliding — and pinned by TestCanonKeepsTheDistinctionsItIsAllowedToKeep, which asserts what canon must equate AND what it must not. L51's sixth instance and the first that erased a distinction symmetrically.

M103-M105 were labelled EQUIVALENT-BY-CONSTRUCTION; they are not equivalent, they are UNREACHED-BY-ANY-TEST. M103 makes RenderSnapshot(map[string]any) raise where CPython renders it fine and M105 makes its output order non-deterministic. A reader who sees 'equivalent' stops looking, which is how r1's M6 got mislabelled one lane over.

nextCycle's doc still opened 'Three lanes' over a five-row table (r1 added the TypeError row, r2 the refusal row), then said 'the middle two' and 'the FOURTH' about rows the opening sentence does not admit exist. Rewritten as four lanes with the two raising rows named as one.

Summary's doc gave a four-row MEASURED table of Python's blanket except whose fourth row is unreachable by construction: _narrate_transition wraps its entire body, import included, in try/except Exception: pass, so the narration loop cannot reach that handler. A claim of measurement over a lane no input produces. Relabelled, and the r3 F1 lane added as a real row.

the package doc justified leaving the snapshot lock to the caller 'because RunCycle does not touch the disk at all' — a reason r1's own restructure falsified, since RunAndPersist performs the load..write. A caller concluding 'nothing here touches the disk, so no lock' reproduces the double-narration race the Python comment exists to prevent. Reason restated against RunAndPersist.

RenderSnapshot's doc said 'R8 pins both halves at once' of the two-different-defaults decision. R8 has ONE process, so its rank is unobservable — sorted() emits the same single line whatever rank it computed. R17 is the fixture that pins the sort half, and battery M80 is invisible to R8.
asDict's doc said the package was asserting v.(pyval.Obj) inline at six sites; it was seven (eight pre-r1, one deliberately left in LoadSnapshot), and there are seven asDict call sites today.

the C38/C39 comment was a parallel construction where C38's numbers described the MESSAGE and C39's described the CLIPPED RESULT: C39's int() message is 240 runes / 439 bytes and clips to 200 runes (359 bytes). A reader recomputing 439 could not reconcile it.

the package doc cited C26 for processes 'still carrying their stale status and evidence'; C26's untouched entry had no evidence key at all. Fixed by adding the evidence to the fixture rather than trimming the doc — the claim was right and the fixture was short.

knowngap_test.go's doc comment opened TestAStringSliceIsALiSTEverywherePyvalSaysItIs for a function spelled ...IsAList...; go doc does not associate the comment and `go test -run` from the comment matches nothing.

title: inspect -summary prints a workspace line cli.py never prints
detail: runInspect printed `workspace: <ws>` and loaded config ABOVE the -summary short-circuit, under a comment reading 'the resolved workspace is printed before any write'. -summary performs no write, so the discipline line leaked into a read-only lane. Found by the both-engines comparison's seventh row, not by a test: the six read-only rows before it were byte-identical.
fix: Moved the print and the config load below the short-circuit. Pinned by a byte-for-byte CLI differential against `cli.py inspector-status` (cmd/maro/inspect_summary_test.go).

title: the empty-inspection string is a different sentence in each engine
detail: Python prints 'No inspection report available. Run maro-inspector first.'; the Go printed 'no inspection recorded yet'. Same state, different prose — the content-key family. Invisible to the comparison because the live workspace holds a report.
fix: Byte-for-byte the Python's sentence; the CLI differential covers an empty workspace as its second case.

title: top_friction_signals decodes to float64, so a count renders in %g
detail: GetLatestInspection used a plain json.Unmarshal, typing every number inside []map[string]any as float64; FrictionSummary interpolated count with %v, which for float64 is %g. Measured: count=2 agrees, count=1000000 renders '1e+06' against CPython's '1000000'. The live workspace holds count=2, which is why the comparison row matched on everything except EC1.
fix: Decode with UseNumber (plus decoderAtEOF, since a Decoder does not inherit Unmarshal's refusal of trailing content) and render with pyval.Str. Twelve fixtures, four of them literals json.loads re-spells (1e21, 1.50, -0, null) so that UseNumber alone cannot carry the test.

title: Realpath refuses any path with a missing intermediate component
detail: Realpath was built on filepath.Abs + EvalSymlinks(parent) + a final-component walk. EvalSymlinks fails outright on a path that is not there, so `<ws>/missing/a/b` returned ok=false where os.path.realpath(strict=False) answers the path itself. The function's OWN doc comment warns that callers read false as 'no such path' and skip work CPython performs. Invisible to the existing differential, whose farm is entirely `<dir>/<name>` — one component, under a directory that exists.
fix: Translated CPython 3.14's posixpath.realpath directly: a part stack, an always-absolute `path`, and a three-state `seen` map. 30-row differential covering missing intermediates, mid-path dangling links, loops, and dot segments.

title: dot-dot was collapsed lexically instead of popping the resolved path
detail: filepath.Abs Cleans, so `..` was applied to the literal input before any symlink was followed. CPython pops the ALREADY-RESOLVED path. With deeplink -> <r>/real/deep, `deeplink/..` is <r>/real in CPython and was <r> here — a different directory, not a different spelling of one.
fix: Same translation; the `..` arm is now CPython's `path[:path.rindex(sep)] or sep` over the resolved path. Pinned by two rows the anti-vacuity check requires CPython to have produced.

title: Workspace() skipped the .resolve() half of workspace_root()
detail: Python is `Path(val).expanduser().resolve()`; the port did expanduser only. A previous round recorded the omission as deliberate, on two grounds that are both measurably false — 'it only changes an answer when a caller chdirs' (no: relative paths, symlinks and dot segments all differ on the first resolution) and 'resolving would make Go disagree with Python about which path string a probe asserts' (backwards). The claim survived because every fixture in the suite set MARO_WORKSPACE to an absolute, symlink-free, already-clean t.TempDir() path.
fix: Env branch resolves; the DEFAULT branch deliberately does not, matching the Python, with its own guard. 19-row differential against workspace_root AND _maro_dir together, since the two differ by exactly that one call.

title: a third private copy of expanduser, built on filepath.Join, which cleans
detail: config.expandUser used filepath.Join, so it removed `..` where Python's Path(val).expanduser() keeps it, and dropped a trailing slash only by accident of Join rather than by pathlib normalisation. Caught by the MARO_USER_DIR trailing-slash row: py '<w>/real', go '<w>/real/'. Workspace() hid it because .resolve() runs afterwards; Home() has no second chance, and Home() is where the user config tier is read from.
fix: Deleted; expandUser is now pypath.Str + pypath.ExpandUser, with the unknown-~user residual unchanged and still named.
